text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Kimmonismus reports AI-enabled attacks on organizations alongside platform breaches and critical software flaws. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6041)

2 — Axios reports U.S. banks found unauthorized AI agents in customer accounts, some apparently acting beyond user instructions. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6042)

3 — Kevin Weil announces Warp Sciences and a $215M Series A to accelerate drug research with AI and robotics. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6043)

4 — Hugging Face's Clement Delangue unveils Carbon-X, an open DNA model, claiming leading open-model benchmark results. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6044)

5 — Anthropic says Claude Security now rescans repositories as code changes, in public beta for Enterprise customers. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6045)

6 — TechCrunch reports Microsoft's diagnostic AI beat generalist doctors in simulations, with most gains from underlying models. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6046)

7 — Rohan Paul reports a DeepMind–Cambridge agent discovered Lean-verified rules for 11 previously unanalyzed Busy Beaver machines. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6047)

8 — A post quotes Anthropic's deputy CIO warning security conditions will worsen and urging boards to fund basic defenses. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6048)

9 — Andrew Curran reports a Quest Diagnostics hack exposed patient data, with an investigation ongoing. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6049)

10 — AtomsNotBits reports Luckey and Lamm launched Warhound with $200M for genetically enhanced defense and emergency-response dogs. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6050)

11 — Rohan Paul reports DeepMind's simulated model auctions achieved 99.2% of the best possible value across prompts. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6051)

12 — TechCrunch reports MIT's 13 AI agents invented games on a virtual island and later generally outperformed unpracticed agents. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6052)

13 — Weil says Warp will build U.S. robotic labs to generate AI training data and support drug developers, not develop drugs itself. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6053)

14 — Citing WSJ, Rohan Paul reports Barclays plans about 5,000 job cuts this year, citing AI efficiency gains. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6054)

15 — A researcher argues automated model training makes original ideas, rather than repeating established recipes, more valuable. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6055)

16 — The channel claims discoveries of security vulnerabilities have been growing exponentially in recent years. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6056)

17 — Mark Gadala reports Oracle issued emergency Java and GraalVM patches for a 9.1-rated, remotely exploitable JSSE flaw. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6057)

18 — The channel urges unique strong passwords, two-factor authentication, and LLM-assisted security checks for software products. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6058)

19 — A post quotes Sam Altman warning AI can uncover hardware-level bugs beyond normal threat models, outpacing patching. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6059)

20 — Jason Clinton urges security leaders to seek board support for basic defenses as he expects conditions to worsen. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6060)

21 — Matt Shumer warns of widespread AI-agent cyberattacks and introduces a guide to protecting individuals and families. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6061)

22 — IntCyberDigest reports Amazon detected a PHP2Shell exploit attempt four days before disclosure, while the flaws were embargoed. (https://t.me/dlmehr/6062)

--Hermes
